title: Proactive Headroom Controller with Fallback Throttles and Per-Model Guarantees
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated expect both per-tenant throughput guarantees and stable latency. Our current autoscaler reacts too slowly to short spikes and is too aggressive during oscillatory workloads, resulting in missed SLAs or large cost swings.

Proposal summary: Implement a two-layer autoscaling policy engine that combines: (1) a predictive headroom allocator that forecasts short-term demand per tenant and per model (60s horizon) and allocates conservative headroom credits, and (2) a reactive fallback throttler that enforces safety limits and graceful degradation when capacity or routing fails. The system will surface per-model guarantees (tokens/sec or requests/sec) and support configurable burst credits, slew-rate limits, and discrete scale steps.

Key features: predictive EWMA+seasonality forecasting, model-aware KV-cache penalties, discrete ramp steps (10% increments), per-tenant minimum floor to preserve baseline SLA, emergency throttles with staged response (reject -> queue -> degrade model variant), and a rollback-safe canary rollout mechanism. Emphasis on observability (token-level accounting, P50/P90/P99 latency, cost delta) and operator controls (pause autoscale, force headroom, manual override).
acceptance_criteria: Predictive allocator produces headroom recommendations every 10s with <=5% repro error in synthetic load tests
Autoscaler can enact discrete scale steps and honour per-tenant floor/ceiling in integration test clusters
Fallback throttler triggers within 5s when node count falls below threshold and transitions through staged responses without data loss
End-to-end e2e test shows P99 latency under guaranteed load within 10% of baseline while cost delta <= +8% in steady-state
Monitoring dashboards created and alerting configured for: missed guarantees, oscillation detection, rollback events, and cost anomalies
tasks: Design doc and API: finalize Confluence design and public autoscale policy schema
Implement forecasting service: lightweight EWMA+seasonal component with per-model tuning
Implement allocator: converts forecasts to headroom credits and recommends scale deltas
Implement reactive throttler: staged degrade paths and emergency quota enforcement
Integrate with existing scaler control loops and deployment orchestration
Add instrumentation: token accounting, burst-credit ledger, and model-variant routing traces
Create e2e test harness and synthetic workload profiles
Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback gates
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Rahman: Kicked off. Draft design posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PROACTIVE-HEADROOM-DESIGN. Goal: balance predictiveness with conservative safety envelope.

2026-02-22 - Mateo Liu: Implemented prototype EWMA forecasting component. Initial tests show accurate short bursts but over-reactive at 1-2 minute periodic workloads. Will add seasonality damping parameter.

2026-02-28 - Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed design. Requested per-model cold-start penalty and opt-in for tenants with small reservations. Also asked to add a config knob for 'aggression' per customer tier.
2026-03-03 - Security review note: No customer data is used in forecasts; only aggregated token counts. Confirmed with security that KMS changes not required. (Security: Ben Ortega)

2026-03-05 - Engineering review: Discussed trade-offs on slew-rate vs discrete steps. Decided to keep discrete 10% steps with a max slew rate of 30% per minute to avoid churn. Follow-up: experiment with fractional micro-steps in fast-path later.

2026-03-08 - QA (Helena Park): Built e2e harness. Synthetic workload profiles attached in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1ProactiveHeadroom/Workloads. Observed oscillation when headroom < 20% for models with cold KV cache.

2026-03-10 - Mateo Liu: PR opened for allocator and throttler core logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Includes unit tests and CI job. Requesting review from runtime and infra teams.
2026-03-12 - Ops (Jorge Mendes): Canary plan approved. Will start 5% fleet canary next week with automated rollback on any P99 latency regression > 15% or missed guarantee events > 2/hour.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit & integration tests in staging with synthetic workloads (complete)
Phase 1: 5% fleet canary for non-critical tenants, monitor 72h
Phase 2: 25% fleet canary including tenants with dedicated SLAs, monitor 7d
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with automated cost/latency gates and manual sign-off
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Forecasting misestimates during sudden traffic pattern shifts -> Mitigation: conservative bias + immediate reactive throttler
Risk: Oscillation due to aggressive scaling -> Mitigation: slew-rate limiter, discrete steps, and move-average dampening
Risk: Increased cost from headroom allocations -> Mitigation: per-tenant config, cost budget alerts, and optional quantization recommendations
Risk: Regression in tail latency for KV-cache sensitive models -> Mitigation: per-model cold-start penalties and warmup migration path
follow_up_actions: Add tenant-level UI controls in Console for aggression and burst credits (PM/UX follow-up)
Run 48h cost experiment with representative customers to measure unit economics impact
Schedule post-canary retro and capture incidents into incident tracker
